messages:
alex: Heads-up — I started seeing a ~15-20% tail latency bump on small-batch traffic after the kernel handoff change we rolled yesterday. Profiling attached below, but interested if others observed the same.

mira: Yep, saw that on canary. P95 for short seqs (<=64) jumped from ~120ms -> ~145ms. Looks like extra kernel launches per request are the culprit.

kevin: Is this the handoff that routes seq<=64 to the arch-optimized fused-kv path? I remember that added a tiny extra launch but reduced FLOPs per token.

alex: Correct — the 1851230000 change. The profiler shows more frequent kernel switches mid-request when continuous batching fills slots. Key counters: kernel_launches increased, avg_launch_ms up.

samir: Can you paste the profiler snippet?

alex: Sure — output excerpt:
```
requests: 10240
seq_bucket: <=64: 76%
batch_window_ms: 8
kernel_path_changes_per_request: median 1 -> 2
kernel_launches_total: 51200 -> 83400
avg_kernel_launch_ms: 0.9 -> 1.6
KV_cache_hit_rate: 97%
````

infra-bot: deploy 1851230000 -> canary (success) :white_check_mark:

mira: The launch overhead is small, but when batching is tiny it doesn't amortize. Continuous batching made more partial batches that cross the handoff boundary.

kevin: Two immediate levers: 1) make scheduler prefer sticky kernel choice for the lifetime of a request if predicted seq_len is small, 2) slightly increase the batching window to amortize launch cost. Both are low-risk.

alex: I did a quick local patch to coalesce kernel launches for first 2 tokens (sticky for first N steps) — p95 dropped to ~125ms in the microbench.

samir: Nice. Also check memory copy patterns: if handoff triggers a fallback path that copies KV caches into a different layout, that could spike per-launch time.

mira: Good call — I saw transient increase in memcpy time correlated with handoffs. I'll run an experiment toggling the cache-layout fallback.

kevin: We should also track a new metric: kernel_handoff_count tagged by seq_len_bucket and batch_size_bucket. We currently have kernel_path but not counts per-request.

alex: Created issue #452 to add kernel_handoff_count and a small autotuner rule: prefer sticky path when predicted handoff_rate > 0.3 for current micro-batch. PR inbound for the metric.

mira: I'll run a focused perf run next: 10k requests, seq<=64, continuous batching on vs off, measure p50/p95/p99 and kernel_launches. Posting numbers in this thread.

samir: Assigning owners: mira -> perf run + writeup, kevin -> metric/alerts + dashboard, alex -> PR for sticky heuristic.

kevin: FYI this shouldn't affect long sequences (seq>512) — handoff codepath isn't used there.

mira: Quick note from the first run: continuous batching ON: p95 144ms, kernel_launches_total 83.4k. OFF: p95 122ms, launches 51.2k. I'll run with the sticky heuristic next.

alex: Thanks — if sticky reduces launches without hurting throughput, we can roll to canary. Also add a promo test on dedicated instances, since reserved pools might have different batching dynamics.

mira: Will do. I'll post detailed numbers and flamegraphs soon.

samir: Thanks everyone. Action items captured in the issue. :thumbsup:
